messages:
sophia: Thinking out loud — proposal for a low-cost rotational canary that stripes probes across capacity lanes. idea is to rotate small, short-lived canaries across different hosts to exercise variants without long-lived pinned sessions. want feedback on tradeoffs.
sophia: sketch: stripe_count=4, probe_window=30s, rotation_period=5m. probes warm caches, collect latency/p95, error rate, and quality hooks.
jamal: +1 for shorter rotations to reduce blast radius. how do we handle session affinity for in-flight requests?
alex: if we rotate often, session affinity will break for long-running chats. we should scope rotational canaries to non-transactional endpoints (stateless generate/embeddings) first.
maria: can we reuse KV cache warmup snapshots? spinning new canaries each rotation is expensive. maybe use a warmup artifact that we transfer with container start.
liam: transferable warmup snapshots sound good but adds complexity to HA. also depends on model variant size + quantization. might be ok as an opt-in optimization.
sophia: agree to start without heavy snapshotting. aim for prefix caching via synthetic probes (short prompts) per rotation. capture top-k tokens to prefill KV.
sophia: question for policy: what roll metrics should gate promote -> full traffic? propose p95 latency delta < 10% AND error rate delta < 0.5% AND eval-quality regression <= 0.5 points on canonical prompts.
jamal: how do we compute "eval-quality" in realtime? we only have periodic evals.
sophia: use two signals — realtime safety/skyline metrics (heuristics) + async evals triggered during rotation. realtime triggers can block promotion, async evals may flip a previously promoted variant back to degraded if regression confirmed.
sophia: also: need a decay window for transient spikes. don't rollback on a single 1-minute spike.
alex: operationally we need a clear control-plane vs runtime boundary. control-plane orchestrates stripe assignments and rotation schedule; runtime must accept stripe-id header and prefer local replicas.
liam: runtime change: add lightweight `X-Canary-Stripe: N` header handling. if header present, do not use long session affinity caches unless warmup token present. fallback path if target host not ready -> route to stable variant.
sophia: yes fallbacks must be automatic and visible. deploy-bot: starting canary rotation might post an ephemeral message with plan and TTL to #eng-oncall.
sre-bot: suggestion: add circuit breaker thresholds per stripe: consecutive_errors >= 5 || p95 > baseline*1.25 => mark stripe unhealthy and skip rotation into that host for N rotations.
jamal: edge-case: noisy neighbors causing transient p95 spikes — we need to correlate with host-level telemetry (cpu/gpu saturation). if host saturated, mark capacity issue not variant issue.
maria: UX: rollout config schema proposal snippet:
```
rollout: 
  mode: rotational
  stripes: 4
  rotation_period: 300s
  probe_window: 30s
  gates:
    latency_p95_delta_pct: 10
    error_rate_delta_pct: 0.5
    quality_regression: 0.5
```
liam: nice. add `affinity_scope: none|short|session` default=short. rotational should default to none or short.
sophia: next steps: I'll write a short RFC follow-up that clarifies runtime API (stripe header), control-plane scheduler, probe workload templates, and gate thresholds. aim to land a prototype in eng-runtime for stateless generate endpoints only.
jamal: can we make stripes deterministic per request token hash so different requests deterministically land on different stripes in target group? that avoids concentrating traffic if upstream LB is sticky.
alex: deterministic assignment is fine but keep it orthogonal to routing policy — control plane can decide to override for testing. document precedence: explicit stripe header > deterministic hash assignment > LB default.
sre-bot: reminder: instrument dashboard panels per stripe: lat/p95, error%, GPU mem, queue depth, and probe quality score. add alerts for stripe-level divergence.
maria: one more thing — rollback semantics: immediate fallback to stable if severe safety violation, otherwise gradual drain and abort promotion. define severity levels in RFC.
sophia: agreed. I'll include sample alert rules + rollback playbook in RFC. tagging @eng-oncall for review after draft. :thumbsup:
sophia: thanks all — I'll post the RFC link when ready and tag for a 30-min sync if folks want to walk it through.
